persona.name: Daniel Suh

occupation.title: Investment Banking Analyst (Second Year Associate Track)
occupation.organization: A mid-market M&A advisory firm in Manhattan
occupation.description: Eighty-hour weeks of models, decks, and client calls. Presentation is part of the job — clients read polish as competence. Skincare started as jet-lag damage control and became a fixed line item.

persona.education: BS in Economics from NYU Stern.
long_term_goals: A one-bedroom in the West Village without a guarantor
Take his parents to Seoul business class
persona.style: Composed, efficient, and quietly status-aware — he speaks in conclusions first, details on request, like a deck summary. Doesn't gush about products; he 'rates' them. Tailored basics, clean fade every two weeks, the watch his dad gave him. Mild embarrassment about how much he spends on skincare, which he covers with irony.

interests: Korean skincare his mom ships him vs the SoHo brands he actually buys
Real estate listings he can't afford yet
likes: Minimalist packaging that looks good on a shelf
dislikes: Being sold to by juniors at counters

beliefs: Presentation compounds — people decide in the first 10 seconds

general: Reorders the same 4 products on subscription
Upgrades one product per quarter after researching like a deal
Gets a facial before big client weeks
Tracks which eye cream survives earnings season

morning: Cleanser, vitamin C, eye cream, SPF moisturizer — 4 minutes flat
workday: Desk by 8:30, deck reviews past midnight in live deals
weekend: Sunday: laundry service pickup, meal delivery, one hour of nothing

health.physical: Fit but chronically under-slept; dark circles and dehydration lines are his stated enemies.
health.mental: High-functioning stress; the marathon training is half therapy.

relationships.name: Grace Suh
relationships.description: Ships him Korean sunscreens with sticky notes; he uses them and doesn't tell his SoHo brands.

relationships.name: Marcus
relationships.description: A teacher in Queens who roasts him for his '$300 face' over monthly KBBQ.
